fields.description:
## Context / Problem

`LLMConfig` (`src/rebar/llm/config.py:473`) exposes `base_url` and `api_key` but no way to
attach request headers, so an operator behind a gateway cannot label rebar's gate calls.
Adding a raw dict is unsafe as-is: both vendor SDKs merge caller headers last, so a
caller-supplied `Authorization` silently displaces the real credential. This ticket adds the
configuration surface and the validation that makes it safe, without yet sending anything.

## Approach

Add `headers: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)` to `LLMConfig`, resolved in
`from_env` by the same three-layer precedence `mcp_servers` already uses at
`src/rebar/llm/config.py:574-594` (CLI `-c llm.headers=<json>` > `REBAR_LLM_HEADERS` JSON >
the `[tool.rebar.llm]` file table). Reusing that resolution shape keeps one documented
precedence story rather than inventing a second.

**Precedence only — deliberately not error handling.** `mcp_servers` silently degrades a
malformed JSON payload to `{}` (`src/rebar/llm/config.py:582-583` and `:593-594`). `headers`
does **not** copy that: a malformed JSON payload in any layer raises `LLMConfigError` naming
the offending layer. Silently dropping headers would leave an operator with an unattributed
gateway and no signal that their configuration was discarded, and it would contradict the
fail-loud rule applied to an unset `${env:VAR}` below. The whole surface gets one fail-loud
story.

Put the value grammar and validation in a new leaf module `src/rebar/llm/headers.py`, so
`config.py` (currently near the module-size policy's comfort range) does not absorb it and
the substitution logic is unit-testable without constructing a config.

Value grammar: a literal string, or a string containing `${env:VAR}` references resolved at
config-resolution time. `${env:...}` uses single braces with an explicit namespace because
`${{ ... }}` is already claimed by the workflow DSL and carries an injection guard
(`src/rebar/llm/workflow/lint_refs.py:5-14`); reusing it would collide with a linter whose
threat model is different. An unset referenced variable is a hard error, matching the
`REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` rule that a missing path never silently degrades
(`src/rebar/llm/config.py:19-21`).

Validation rejects, with a named `LLMConfigError`:
- header names in the denied set `authorization`, `x-api-key`, `cookie`, `host`,
  `proxy-authorization` (case-insensitive) — these forge or displace authentication;
- header names outside RFC 7230 token characters;
- values containing CR, LF, or NUL.

A denylist rather than an allowlist: arbitrary gateway header names are the point of the
feature, so an allowlist would defeat it. The threat being closed is credential displacement
and protocol injection, both of which are closed sets.

`${run:...}` references are recognized by the grammar but left unresolved here; the
delivery ticket resolves them.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — the `headers` field and its three-layer resolution in `from_env`.
- `src/rebar/llm/headers.py` (new) — grammar, `${env:...}` resolution, name/value validation.
- `tests/unit/test_llm_headers.py` (new) — the tests below.

## Testing

Tier: in-process unit tests against the real functions — the mechanism is pure string
resolution and validation with no boundary to cross, so no higher tier is warranted.

- Happy path: a literal header and an `${env:VAR}` header both resolve, the latter from a
  monkeypatched environment.
- Failure paths: each denied header name; a name with an invalid character; values containing
  CR, LF and NUL; an `${env:VAR}` naming an unset variable; a malformed JSON
  payload in the env layer and in the CLI layer.
- Negative control: a header named `x-authorization-context` is accepted, proving the denylist
  matches exact names and does not substring-match legitimate ones.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `LLMConfig.headers` defaults to an empty dict, so an unconfigured deployment is
      byte-unchanged; checked by `test_headers_default_empty` asserting
      `LLMConfig.from_env().headers == {}` with no relevant env set.
- [ ] Headers resolve from all three layers with CLI > env > file precedence; checked by a
      test setting all three and asserting the CLI value wins, mirroring the `mcp_servers`
      precedence test.
- [ ] A `${env:VAR}` value resolves from the environment; checked by a test monkeypatching
      `VAR` and asserting the resolved header equals its value.
- [ ] An `${env:VAR}` naming an unset variable raises `LLMConfigError` naming the variable;
      checked by `pytest.raises` asserting the variable name appears in the message.
- [ ] Each of `authorization`, `x-api-key`, `cookie`, `host`, `proxy-authorization` is
      rejected case-insensitively with `LLMConfigError`; checked by a parametrized test over
      the five names in three casings.
- [ ] A header value containing CR, LF or NUL is rejected with `LLMConfigError`; checked by a
      parametrized test over the three characters.
- [ ] A malformed JSON payload in the env layer or the CLI layer raises `LLMConfigError`
      naming that layer, rather than degrading to an empty dict; checked by a parametrized
      test over both layers asserting the raise and the layer name in the message.
- [ ] A header named `x-authorization-context` is accepted; checked by a test asserting it
      survives validation, proving exact-name rather than substring matching.
